verification_method: Direct HTTP requests against each endpoint. No source was assumed to work from documentation alone.

sources.name: Epoch AI — AI Benchmarking Hub

license.citation: Epoch AI, 'AI Benchmarking Hub'. Published online at epoch.ai. Retrieved from 'https://epoch.ai/benchmarks'

notes: Files without the '_external' suffix are evaluations Epoch runs itself and publishes inspect logs for; these are first-hand third_party_benchmark data.
Files ending in '_external' are aggregated from elsewhere and carry 'Source' and 'Source link' columns; propagate that provenance instead of crediting Epoch.
'Model accessibility' distinguishes 'API access' / 'Open weights' / 'Open weights (non-commercial)' and is the cleanest open-vs-closed signal found in any source.
'Country' enables the China-vs-US framing the project explicitly wants, without us having to maintain that mapping by hand.
epoch_capabilities_index.csv is Epoch's own composite (ECI). Do NOT feed it into our composite: it would double-count its constituent benchmarks. Useful only as an external cross-check.

sources.name: LMArena (Arena) — Leaderboard Dataset

access.format: parquet (also readable as JSON rows via the HF datasets-server REST API)
access.rate_limit: anonymous HF limits apply; exact quota unverified

license.evidence: license:cc-by-4.0 tag on the HF dataset API response

sources.update_cadence: irregular; several publishes per month, not daily (no rows exist for 2026-07-01 or 2026-07-15)

provides.history_depth: full split carries every historical snapshot; a single model had 61 dated observations

notes: The 'full' split is the one to ingest: it gives the complete time series for free, which is exactly what history.jsonl and the sparklines need.
The 'license' column ('Proprietary' vs open licenses) is an independent cross-check against Epoch's 'Model accessibility'.

Rating system changed from Elo to Bradley-Terry on 2024-01-09; style control became default for text/vision on 2025-05-16; frequency re-weighting added 2025-07-23. Pre-2024 values are not comparable to current ones.
caveats: VERIFIED ANOMALY: the newest snapshot (2026-07-21) returns 1113 rows for category='overall' across 378 distinct models (~3x duplication), with rank=1 appearing three separate times and divergent ratings per model. The 2026-06-04 snapshot is clean at 365 rows. Ingest MUST deduplicate and MUST sanity-check the rows/distinct-models ratio, falling back to the last clean snapshot when the ratio exceeds ~1.2.
The 'latest' split inherits the same anomaly. Prefer 'full' + max(leaderboard_publish_date) after the sanity check.

sources.name: LiveBench

license.evidence: LICENSE file at LiveBench/LiveBench is the Apache License 2.0, carried over from lm-sys/FastChat. Verified 2026-07-27; the GitHub API's NOASSERTION was a false alarm caused by the FastChat preamble.

notes: The CSV ships raw per-task scores with no precomputed aggregate. We compute the category averages ourselves from categories_{date}.json, which makes the whole chain reproducible by hand from public files — exactly what /methodology promises.
LiveBench refreshes its questions to resist training-data contamination, which is why it earns a slot despite the smaller model count.
The HuggingFace datasets under the 'livebench' org are question sets last touched 2025-04, NOT the leaderboard. Do not ingest them.
caveats: Snapshot discovery is the weak point: the list of available snapshot dates lives in a JS array inside https://livebench.ai/static/js/main.{hash}.js, and the hash changes on every deploy. Ingest must resolve index.html -> bundle URL -> date array -> newest date, and fall back to the last known-good snapshot on failure.

sources.name: SWE-bench

access.rate_limit: GitHub raw limits; generous for one daily fetch
access.robots_txt: Contains only Cloudflare content-signal explanatory comments and no actual directives; no restriction is expressed.

license.evidence: LICENSE file at SWE-bench/swe-bench.github.io (the repo that serves data/leaderboards.json) is 'Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International'. Verified 2026-07-27.
license.conflict: Incompatible with shipping the data inside an MIT-licensed repository: MIT grants commercial reuse that CC-BY-NC-4.0 withholds. Anyone forking ModelHub would inherit data they cannot use commercially.

sources.last_observed_update: newest Verified entry dated 2026-02-26; website repo last pushed 2026-03-29
sources.update_cadence: irregular; effectively frozen for ~5 months as of verification
notes: 'os_model' and 'os_system' give open-source flags for the model and the agent scaffold separately.
'resolved' is a percentage; 'cost' is total USD for the run, which is useful editorial context.
caveats: BLOCKING: the data is CC-BY-NC-4.0 and this repository is MIT. Do not commit swebench.com data to /data until a human decides. Recommended resolution: drop the swebench.com ingest and rely on Epoch's own CC-BY-4.0 swe_bench_verified.csv, which already carries the Coding weight; keep swebench.com as an outbound reference link only. This costs nothing in the composite.

RULE: SWE-bench never contributes a bare-model score to the composite. Epoch's swe_bench_verified.csv is what weighs in Coding. If SWE-bench entries are ever displayed, the agent scaffold must be visible in the UI.

Entries identify an agent+model scaffold, not a bare model — e.g. 'live-SWE-agent + Claude 4.5 Opus medium (20251101)' or 'Sonar Foundation Agent + Claude 4.5 Opus'. Mapping these onto canonical model ids is genuinely ambiguous and is the main reason aliases.json needs to exist. Attributing a scaffold's score to a bare model would itself be a form of bias, so the UI must disclose the scaffold.
Epoch also publishes swe_bench_verified.csv from its own runs. Prefer Epoch's when both cover the same model, and keep this source for breadth.
